newsitem.title: UK: LCE cocoa ends weaker in active selling.
newsitem.headline: LCE cocoa ends weaker in active selling.

text.p: London cocoa futures extended losses in active afternoon deals on Wednesday as mixed selling pushed prices to the edge of key support, traders said.
Some traders attributed the sales to funds while others said liquidation by trade houses was responsible for the losses.
"Funds are throwing the money around. London seems to be in a pattern as a good seller," said one.
But another said: "Perhaps one of the larger traders with forecasting teams in Ivory Coast have foreseen a good crop. It is hard to tell but I don't know if it is just funds."
The key second-month December contract closed at 990 stg a tonne, down 10 stg on the day, after hitting a session low of 985 stg. Front-month September lost four stg to end at 970 stg a tonne.
Traders said switches were reasonably active with March/May at 14 stg, and Sept/Dec at 24-25 stg and Dec/March at 10, 11 and 12 stg.
One trader said arbitrage between New York and London had got out of line as a result of a stronger market in New York buoyed by trade buying.
"There is no reason why New York should have picked up," he said.
Technical analysts have said earlier that support was likely to hold around the 995-980 stg area on December.
UK crop analyst PCR Limited, led by Robert Fish, is expected to release its updated Ivorian forecast later this week.
Ivorian output prospects are said to have improved slightly after the crop escaped damage from heavy rains in early July but pod setting remains unimpressive, crop analysts said.
